_note: Skills come from 2-framework/framework-v3/padel-iq-skills.csv via npm run import-framework. Edit the CSV, not this file.

axes.name: Movement
axes.short: Position, recovery, moving as a pair

levels.name: Beginner
levels.description: Learning the rules and the court. Getting the ball over the net is the main challenge.
levels.coachFocus: Learn the rules and where to stand. Get the serve in and the ball over the net.

levels.name: D
levels.description: Consistent basics: you return reliably, serve in, and keep a simple rally going.
levels.coachFocus: Get it back. Keep the ball in play. No need for winners.

levels.name: C
levels.description: Controlled shots in friendly games: lobs, bandeja, basic glass play.
levels.coachFocus: Be consistent, and start aiming for spaces: the sides and the middle.

levels.name: B
levels.description: Reliable in matches: wins points on purpose, handles pressure.
levels.coachFocus: Build points on purpose: use depth, pace and height to move opponents, then finish when the ball is there.

levels.name: A
levels.description: Complete player: varied shots, smart tactics, and stays strong against good opponents.
levels.coachFocus: Control the match: vary spin and pace, read the opponents and change the plan when needed.

levels.name: Pro
levels.description: Professional level. The top benchmark, not an assessment target for most players.

rules._note: Draft rules from design chats. Not final.

levelPass.note: OPEN: all items, or most (placeholder 4 out of 5, no big gaps).

rules.axisLevel: Highest level whose master skills the player passes, worked out per axis.
rules.overallLevel: OPEN: not decided. Simple option: where most axes sit. Shown smaller than the pentagon.
rules.pushingAhead: A skill is 'pushing ahead' when the player's level is below the skill's first master level. It never raises or lowers their level.
rules.unratedSkills: Skills not yet rated are excluded from the calculation. They are not counted as D.
rules.plusLevels: OPEN: 'D+' could mean passed D and working through the C list. No minus levels.

journalPrompts: One thing to try next match?

statementCheck.rule: A player has a level for a skill when they are good enough at that level's statements (about 3 in 4 'usually' or 'always') AND have mastered every level below it (about 3 in 4 'always').
statementCheck.note: Agreed with Richard 26 Oct: mastery = always, good enough = usually. The 3-in-4 share is a placeholder.

quickCheck.how: Player picks the level they think they are. App asks 2 statements at that level, 1 warning sign for that level, and 1 stretch statement from the level above.

outcomes.solid_close: Good enough at the level, warning rare, stretch usually/always
outcomes.solid: Good enough at the level, warning rare
outcomes.not_solid: One weak answer at the level, or the warning happens sometimes
outcomes.lower: Not good enough at the level, or the warning happens often

quickCheck.playerDecides: If the answers suggest a lower level, the player chooses to keep their level (marked 'set by you') or switch.

rules.optional: Optional rows and skills are never required: they are left out of both sides of any level sum, never cap a level, and checking more optional shots never raises a level.
